newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Benguet gets one-year debt moratorium.
newsitem.headline: Benguet gets one-year debt moratorium.

text.p: Benguet Corp, which used to be one of the country's biggest gold mining firms, has secured a one-year debt moratorium on principal payments worth 944 million pesos, a senior company official said on Tuesday.
The moratorium, which will expire in the first quarter next year, was given by 19 local and foreign banks, he told reporters, but declined to be identified.
The official said the firm requested relief from banks because of the losses incurred last year.
Benguet swung to a net loss of 165.1 million pesos in 1996 from a profit of 40.2 million in 1995.

The company suffered from unfavourable metal prices and poor production due to calamities and opposition by militant small-scale miners which made it difficult for the firm to access its mines in the north.
"For this year, it will be another loss," said company president Dennis Belmonte.
Officials said the company hopes to get an additional $85 million next year to pay off its debts.

The money is expected to come from Echo Bay Mines and TVI Pacific Inc when they exercise their option to develop the Kingking copper and gold mine in Pinatukan, Davao del Norte province in southern Philippines, officials said.
Belmonte, in his report to stockholders, said the latest study on the Kingking mine showed higher reserves.
"Ore reserves have increased to more than 529 million tonnes at a lower grade of 0.35 percent total copper and 0.41 grams of gold per tonne," he said.
An earlier study by the company indicated ore reserves of 315 million tonnes at a grade of 0.44 percent total copper and 0.52 grams of gold per tonne.
